saw.short: An I'm A Celebrity camp row sparks a big conversation
saw.headline: An *I’m A Celebrity camp row* sparks a big conversation
saw.what: On Sunday’s episode Mariella Frostrup, 64, called AJ Odudu “aggressive” and “dramatic” during a camp cooking row, and AJ replied “Please don’t use that word”. Mariella later apologised, per LADbible and Metro. ITV said duty of care is “of the utmost importance” and that production monitors camp 24/7, per Deadline. Metro reports bosses spoke to Mariella, but ITV’s statement doesn’t confirm it.
saw.why: The biggest TV talking point of the week. Tone matters, so we keep to the facts.
saw.source: Metro, 23 Nov; LADbible, 23 Nov; Deadline, 23 Nov

saw.short: The UK is confirmed as 2035 Women's World Cup host
saw.headline: The *UK is confirmed as 2035 Women’s World Cup host*
saw.what: Fifa confirmed England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales as joint hosts of the 2035 Women’s World Cup on Monday, per BBC Sport and Sky Sports. It is the first football World Cup in the UK since the men’s tournament in 1966. The bid proposes 19 venues, with 104 matches, 48 teams and 39 days.
saw.why: A big, positive sport story for the whole UK. Long runway for brand moments.
saw.source: BBC Sport, 23 Nov; Sky Sports, 23 Nov

saw.headline: *Avengers: Doomsday* final trailer drops ahead of 18 December
saw.what: The final Avengers: Doomsday trailer arrived on Monday, ahead of the 18 Dec release, per Variety. In it Robert Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom says “All of you have lived stolen lives”, per Deadline. Variety’s date is for the release generally. We haven’t checked UK-specific dates.
saw.why: A Disney and Marvel moment. Trailer day is a social peak for film brands.

saw.short: Strictly confirms Instant Dance returns for week 10
saw.headline: Strictly confirms *Instant Dance* returns for week 10
saw.what: Johannes Radebe confirmed on Sunday’s results show that the Instant Dance challenge returns on Saturday 28 Nov, per Radio Times. Each couple picks a dance style at random, makes a quick costume change, and has 10 seconds to decide how to dance it. Radio Times says it caused “chaos and costume changes” last year.
saw.why: A format everyone remembers. Fans will make predictions all week.

saw.short: Which? says one in five Black Friday deals was a genuine bargain
saw.headline: *Which?* says just one in five Black Friday deals was a genuine bargain
saw.what: Which? tracked 756 home, tech and health appliances at eight retailers and found only 22% of Black Friday 2025 discounts were the lowest price of the year. Retail Gazette reports Vouchernaut data that found 2,300 products had been cheaper in the 24 days before the sales. This is last year’s data. Black Friday is on Fri 27 Nov.
saw.why: Shoppers are sceptical before the sale. It shapes how deals land on social.

saw.short: A Cornwall Christmas market looks nothing like its apparent AI posters
saw.headline: A Cornwall *Christmas market* looks nothing like its apparent AI posters
saw.what: The Kernow Christmas Market in Redruth opened in a sparsely decorated warehouse, and visitors compared it to the Willy Wonka Experience, per Metro and LADbible. Its promo images appeared to be AI-generated, though we haven’t seen a statement from the organisers. The funfair was shut on Sunday for high winds. Traders paid from £30 a day, per Metro.
saw.why: A lesson in expectation versus reality. Fake-looking posters now spread fast.

platform.short: Pinterest opens its ad inventory to Microsoft Advertising campaigns
platform.headline: *Pinterest* opens its ad inventory to Microsoft Advertising campaigns
platform.what: Pinterest’s open-auction inventory across home feed, search and related Pins can now be reached from Microsoft Advertising campaigns, per Pinterest’s newsroom and Social Media Today. Pinterest quotes 661 million monthly active users and 80 billion monthly searches, with more than half showing commercial intent. These are Pinterest’s own figures.
platform.why: More ways for advertisers to buy Pinterest. Useful for retail and home clients.
platform.source: Pinterest Newsroom, 23 Nov; Social Media Today, 23 Nov

platform.short: Pinterest puts teen parental controls on one page
platform.headline: *Pinterest* puts teen parental controls on one page
platform.what: Pinterest has put parental controls in one place and added settings for the amount of AI-generated content, notification volume and video autoplay, per its UK newsroom and Social Media Today. Every setting is locked by a parental passcode. It links to device-level screen time and location settings on iOS and Android.
platform.why: A teen-safety update with a UK page. Good to know for family-facing brands.
platform.source: Pinterest Newsroom UK, 23 Nov; Social Media Today, 23 Nov

platform.headline: *Threads* previews an iPad app
platform.what: Threads head of design Christopher Clare posted screenshots of the feed on an iPad, with no release date, per Social Media Today. iPad users currently use a browser or the iPhone app. We haven’t seen Clare’s original post.
platform.why: A sign Threads is building for bigger screens. Nothing live yet.
